rationale: Salesforce ISV developers building AppExchange managed packages are a specific, named B2B buyer with real security review costs ($5–20k for Salesforce Security Review consultants) — willingness to pay and buyer clarity are both solid. Claude can generate an Apex file-validation code template or security checklist report with high buildability. However, the total (5.9) sits below the build threshold (6.5), and operational_autonomy at 6 just barely clears its gate floor — the niche is narrow enough that lead volume may be thin, and Youval lacks a specific Salesforce domain edge. Validate before building.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a Salesforce Apex File Upload Security Audit Pack: a Salesforce ISV developer submits their managed package context (endpoint type, user type, file types accepted) via a form, and Claude generates a tailored Apex code template with server-side validation logic, an OWASP-aligned security checklist, and a written security narrative ready to paste into a Salesforce Security Review submission. BUILD: A simple intake form + Claude prompt trained on Salesforce Apex security patterns + Stripe payment link at ~$149/report + automated file/email delivery — no coding by Youval. SELL: Reach Salesforce ISV developers via Salesforce Partner Community forums, the Salesforce Developers Slack, and AppExchange Partner Program mailing lists — the factory drafts outreach, Youval approves before sending. MAINTAIN: Intake → Claude generation → delivery → billing runs automatically; Youval reviews outreach batches. Validate with 5 free reports in the Salesforce Partner Community in exchange for feedback before charging.
notes: All build gates technically pass (operational_autonomy=6 meets floor=6 exactly; buildability=6 meets floor=6; buyer_clarity=7 meets floor=6; willingness_to_pay=7 meets floor=5), but total 5.9 is below min_total_to_build (6.5), so stage is validate by threshold. The niche is genuinely narrow — there may be only a few hundred active Salesforce ISV developers globally, which limits ceiling but also limits competition.
